text.p: Adelaide broker Day Cutten Ltd has forecast a 5.6 percent drop in net earnings before abnormals in 1996/97 (June 30) for technology company Vision Systems Ltd to A$10.0 million due to key product delays.

The broker has issued a hold recommendation for the stock, A$10 a share at the time of writing (A$11.0 for convertible notes), saying a number of acqusitions may be announced this year which would drive earnings growth over the next three years. The stock was at A$9.10 at the close on Tuesday.
Vision Systems reported a A$10.64 million net profit for 1995/96, up from A$9.14 million in the previous year.

Writing in Day Cutten's annual South Australian Companies Review, published this week, analyst Nick Ross said the nature and quality of the possible acquisitions would determine Vision System's short-term share price performance.
"The convertible notes remain attractive for income conscious investors with a running yield of around 10.4 percent," he said.
Ross said Vision Systems had experienced delays in the launch of the VESDA 'Laser Plus' smoke detector and the 'Storewatch' video security system.
But significant profit growth was expected in 1997/98 as the new products became established in the market and the revenue impact of new acquisitions became apparent, he said.
He forecast a rise in net profit before abnormals to A$14 million in 1997/98, with revenues rising to A$130 million from an anticipated A$95 million in 1996/97.
On a two to three year view, Ross said revenues of around A$16 million were anticipated from the LADS (laser airborne depth sounder) contract with the United States Navy.
